How to Apply
1: Submit Application Form
Once you create an account, you will select the application form for your intended program. You are encouraged to complete this short form in one sitting but may save and return later. The form takes about 15 minutes to complete. Uploading supporting documents and recommendation letters is done at a later stage.
Already have a Graduate AU Admissions Portal account? Login here.
International Applicants: before applying please review International Requirements.
2: Pay Application Fee
As part of the application form submission, the system will apply a nonrefundable $55 application fee required at this stage to access the supplemental items section. Fee waivers are reserved for recruitment event or webinar attendees.
3: Upload Required Materials
Submit all required materials as early as possible to allow time for them to be received. After admittance, you will be required to mail all official transcripts (see last FAQ below for mailing address). Received documents are not returnable or transferable.
Personal statements generated solely by Artificial Intelligence (AI) products are not appropriate for admission applications. By submitting your application, you are confirming the Statement of Purpose was authored by you, the applicant. For guidance on writing your Statement of Purpose, please visit our Events Page for upcoming webinars and info sessions.

Combining Bachelor's and Master's Programs
Current undergraduate students at AU have the option of combining their bachelor's and master's degrees. Students admitted to a Combined Bachelor-to-Master's degree may share between 9-12 credits between the degree levels, depending on the total credits for the Master's degree.
As a current AU student, consider these next steps:
Decide which master's programs are of interest and create an account in the graduate application portal for the affiliated AU Graduate School;
Meet with a graduate admissions advisor at the school hosting the program to learn about the graduate programs and ask if there are graduate faculty members you may speak with;
Discuss your interest with a current supportive faculty member. They may provide your recommendation;
Meet with your undergraduate academic advisors to learn the courses appropriate for the program of interest.
